fields.name: value
fields.documentation: A typed temperature value. Statement leaves that observe, assert or impose a temperature inherit this `value`. Series-as-cardinality (Brainstorm I): an ARRAY of the composite; a single reading is the length-1 case. Per-sample timing is a time covariate along a time dimension: in the statement's `dimensions` and `covariates` when inline, on each body's when stored in a body (#73 item 21; keys until 2026-10-22, data_body plan AMENDMENT 6). NEW NUMERIC SHAPE (did_v2_numeric_shape_plan.md [one shape for measured numbers], Jess Haley, 2026-11-17, section 8 answer 4): a series is ONE cell whose canonical field and `source_numeric` are arrays, with one `source_unit`, one `approximate` and one `tolerance`; an array of cells of one number each, with `source_value`, is the OLD SHAPE, read until the readers drop it (section 9, step 4).

fields.name: celsius
fields.documentation: Canonical temperature value -- the normalised, cross-document comparable number. Absent only when the run's migration report lists it as a gap ([gap accepted when the report lists it]; the source gave no unit, or a unit with no conversion; `source_value` and `source_unit` keep what the source wrote) -- Jess Haley 2026-10-30 [canonical absent only as needs info].

fields.name: source_unit
fields.documentation: The unit the source gave the value in, as a term: the unit's registered term (schemas/registry/did_v2_term_registry.json), its label as the name (did_v2_source_unit_plan.md). Blank when the source gives no unit.

fields.name: source_value
fields.documentation: OLD SHAPE: read until the readers drop it (did_v2_numeric_shape_plan.md section 9, step 4), then removed by did-schema ([one shape for measured numbers]). The writers write the new shape (DID-matlab #473, NDI-matlab #1258). Was: The number as given by the source, in `source_unit`.

fields.name: source_numeric
fields.documentation: The number as given by the source, in `source_unit` (`source_value` renamed; did_v2_numeric_shape_plan.md [one shape for measured numbers], Jess Haley, 2026-11-17, section 2). One number, as the canonical field is, except in a statement's own `value`: there a series is ONE cell whose canonical field and `source_numeric` are arrays, with one `source_unit`, one `approximate` and one `tolerance` (section 8 answer 4; [series readings share a source record]). A nested reference to this class (a time reference's `start`, a dose's `mass`) holds one number. The field is declared scalar because the two uses share this declaration; DID-matlab did2.schema.numericShapeFields marks the statement value's series.

fields.name: approximate
fields.documentation: True when the value is approximate.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.documentation: The bound on this value: the true value lies between `value - minus` and `value + plus`, in the canonical unit (celsius). Asymmetric when the uncertainty is one-sided (a clock time written to the minute is minus 0 / plus 59 s). ABSENT means no tolerance is stated. A bound, not a standard deviation (CHANGE 7).

fields.name: minus
fields.documentation: How far BELOW the stated value the true value may lie, in the canonical unit (celsius) (for a time: how much EARLIER). Non-negative.

fields.name: plus
fields.documentation: How far ABOVE the stated value the true value may lie, in the canonical unit (celsius) (for a time: how much LATER). Non-negative.
